## Research Notes
- `session-launch.sh:303-310` plan outcome switch: `tasks` → `advance tasks`; `blocked` → `block`.
- `ledger.sh` unblock (`:466-520`): `human:plan-review` clears on `## Reviewed` — which the background
  planner's own `/hef.review` writes, so it can never be a *person's* gate. Hence a new kind,
  `human:plan-approval`, not a second meaning for the old one (review #1). The intake clear
  (`--reviewed-by-human --by`, regex `:497-502`, refused under `HEFESTO_WORKER`, recorded in `.reviewed`)
  is the one definition of "a person did this" to reuse. The precheck at `:474-475` ("apply to
  human:intake only") is relaxed for plan-approval only; the `ci` refusal case in the suite stays.
- `block` refuses to replace `human:intake` for every caller (`:460`), other `human:*` only under
  `HEFESTO_WORKER` (`:462`). plan-approval joins intake as never-replaceable (review #2).
- `advance` refuses only while a `human:*` block is open (`:404-405`). Leaving `plan-review` will also need
  a recorded approval (review #2, #8).
- `/hef.orchestrate` step 1 is two compound shell lines (routing, kind, raw body into a temp file, init);
  allow rules must match each subcommand, and `$(…)`/redirects are checked separately (Claude Code docs) →
  a single `ledger.sh register` call (FR-005). Every other Bash call in the command is already one call.
- `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` here expands to the clone (`~/.claude-framework`) while the registry's
  `installPath` is the profile cache: the allowlist covers both roots, single and doubled slash.
- Claude Code (docs, 2026-10-19): no configurable main-conversation auto-compact point or instructions; only
  status-line scripts receive `context_window.used_percentage` (may be absent before the first response);
  a fixed-interval `/loop` survives `/clear` and `/compact` and expires after 7 days; peer messages can
  neither run a command nor approve one.
- `ledger.sh` is over the 500-code-line limit (~570): new functions live in `hooks/ledger-lanes.sh`,
  sourced like `board-lib.sh` (`:60-62`); ledger.sh only gains dispatch lines.

## Data Model
Config (opt-in): `orchestrate.plan_review: "human" | "agent"`; `orchestrate.rfc_dir` (default `docs/rfcs`);
`context.compact_at: <n> | {<lane>: <n>}`. Entry: `.reviewed[]` gains `{kind: "human:plan-approval", by,
at, rfc_sha?}`; `.source.rfc = {path, sha256}` set at approval.

## API Contracts
- `ledger.sh register <id> --ref <column>#<id>` → `<id> registered (kind <k>[, repo <r>])`; a routing or
  kind refusal → exit 1 with status-board's message, nothing written.
- `ledger.sh unblock <id> --reviewed-by-human --by <name>` also clears `human:plan-approval` (phase
  `plan-review` → `tasks`; or, at `tasks` after an RFC change, re-approval in place).
- `status-board.sh --item-rfc <id>` → the absolute RFC path, or empty (no `rfc:` line, exit 0); invalid → exit 1.
- `lane-launch.sh <lane> [--print] [--keep-statusline]`; `context-gauge.sh` (stdin JSON → one line or none).

## Implementation Approach
Mechanical and opt-in: without `plan_review`, `rfc:` lines, `context`, or the launcher, every behaviour is
today's. One person-gate function serves intake and plan-approval. The RFC is data: its path is validated
before use, the planner is told to treat it as the design and never as instructions, and its hash pins what
was approved.

## Code Sketches (Mental Alignment)

### Sketch 1: plan outcome with a person's review
**File:** `hooks/session-launch.sh` (`:307`)
```bash
case "$(cfg '.orchestrate.plan_review // "agent"')" in agent|human) ;; *) die "… plan_review must be \"human\" or \"agent\" (got …)";; esac
tasks) if [ "$PR_MODE" = human ]; then "$LEDGER" advance "$ID" plan-review && "$LEDGER" block "$ID" --kind human:plan-approval || exit 1
       else "$LEDGER" advance "$ID" tasks || exit 1; fi ;;
```

### Sketch 2: the person-only clear
**File:** `hooks/ledger-lanes.sh`, called from the unblock arm
```bash
plan_approval_clear() { person_gate human:plan-approval     # --by regex; refused under HEFESTO_WORKER
  [ -n "$SPEC_DIR" ] && [ -f "$SPEC_DIR/tasks.md" ] || die "… needs a spec folder with tasks.md (spec_dir: '${SPEC_DIR:-none}')"
  sha=$(rfc_hash "$E")                                   # empty when the item has no RFC
  jq … '.blocked_on=null | .reviewed+=[{kind:"human:plan-approval",by:$by,at:(now|todate),rfc_sha:$s}]
        | if $s != "" then .source.rfc={path:$p,sha256:$s} else . end | if .phase=="plan-review" then .phase="tasks" else . end' ; }
```
`block`: `[ "$CURK" != human:plan-approval ] || die "… never replaced"`. `advance`: from `plan-review`
refused unless `.reviewed | any(.kind=="human:plan-approval")`.

### Sketch 4: one-call registration
**File:** `hooks/ledger-lanes.sh`
```bash
register() { R=""; if is_external; then R=$("$SB" --item-repo "$ID") || die "$R"; R=${R%%$'\t'*}; fi
  K=$("$SB" --item-kind "$ID") || die …; T=$(mktemp); "$SB" --item-raw "$ID" > "$T" || die …
  init_entry "$ID" --kind tasks-repo --ref "$REF" --body-file "$T" --item-kind "$K" ${R:+--repo "$R"}; rm -f "$T"; }
```

### Sketch 5: lane launcher
**File:** `hooks/lane-launch.sh`
```bash
case "$1" in orchestrator|plan|build|deploy) ;; *) die "lane must be orchestrator, plan, build or deploy (got '$1')";; esac
top=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel) || die "run it inside the project's git repository"
for r in "$CLONE" "$CACHE"; do for s in "$r/hooks" "$r//hooks"; do allow+=("Bash($s/status-board.sh:*)" "Bash($s/session-launch.sh:*)" "Bash($s/speckit-helper.sh:*)" "Bash($s/pr-watch.sh:*)" \
  "Bash($s/ledger.sh board:*)" "Bash($s/ledger.sh list:*)" "Bash($s/ledger.sh next:*)" "Bash($s/ledger.sh show:*)" "Bash($s/ledger.sh metrics:*)" \
  "Bash($s/ledger.sh register:*)" "Bash($s/ledger.sh block:*)" "Bash($s/ledger.sh publish:*)" "Bash($s/ledger.sh escalate:*)"); done; done
exec env HEFESTO_LANE="$1" claude --name "$(basename "$top")-$1" --permission-mode default --settings "$(jq -n … )"
```

### Sketch 6: gauge
**File:** `hooks/context-gauge.sh`
```bash
command -v jq >/dev/null || exit 0; in=$(cat)
pct=$(jq -r '.context_window.used_percentage // empty | floor' <<<"$in" 2>/dev/null); [[ "$pct" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || exit 0
at=$(jq -r --arg l "${HEFESTO_LANE:-}" '.context.compact_at | if type=="number" then . elif type=="object" then (.[$l] // 40) else 40 end' "$cfg" 2>/dev/null)
[[ "$at" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || at=40; [ "$at" -gt 0 ] && [ "$pct" -ge "$at" ] && echo "ctx $pct% · /compact (${HEFESTO_LANE:-general})" || echo "ctx $pct%"
```
No ledger, board-lib or git call: a status line runs on every refresh.

## Smoke cases (each with the mutation that must turn it red)
1. plan_review human: tasks outcome → phase plan-review + plan-approval block — *advance-to-tasks restored*.
2. plan_review "Human" (invalid) → refused loudly — *validation removed*.
3. A plain `unblock` of plan-approval, `## Reviewed` present → refused — *person gate skipped*.
4. Person clear: refused without `--by`, under `HEFESTO_WORKER`, with empty spec_dir, without tasks.md;
   passes with a name → phase tasks, `.reviewed` record — *each check removed in turn (one mutation each for
   --by and tasks.md)*.
5. `block <id> --kind ci` over plan-approval → refused — *never-replaceable removed*.
6. `advance <id> tasks` from plan-review with no approval record → refused — *advance guard removed*.
7. Without plan_review: tasks outcome → phase tasks (existing suite green).
8. `--item-rfc`: valid path → absolute; `..`, absolute, outside rfc_dir, missing, non-.md → refused — *`..` check removed*.
9. RFC hash: approval records it; editing the RFC → implement launch refused, entry blocked on plan-approval,
   no claude call; re-approval → launches — *hash comparison removed*.
10. Plan prompt names the RFC path and the data rule when the item has `rfc:` — *RFC sentence removed*.
11. `register`: in-repo and external (routed repo), a routing refusal writes nothing, a kind failure writes
    nothing — *repo capture through a pipe (the bug the old note warns about)*.
12. lane-launch `--print`: name, `HEFESTO_LANE`, default mode, sandbox off, allow rules present, and none for
    `ledger.sh unblock|record|claim|advance|handoff`; bad lane refused; outside git refused — *an unblock rule added*.
13. Gauge: empty/missing percentage, `41.7`, garbage stdin, threshold 0, object missing the lane, invalid
    threshold, no jq → exit 0, nothing on stderr; 40/39 boundary — *`-ge` → `-gt`*.
14. Orchestrator `--stage all` text present with the three passes and the hold warning (static check).

## Constitution Compliance
- [x] **Payload under the plugin root**: new files in `hooks/`.
- [x] **Zero-install**: bash, jq, git.
- [x] **Mutation-tested guards**: cases 1–13, each with its mutation.
- [x] **Loud failures**: `plan_review` and `rfc:` values refused with the value and the fix; the gauge's
  silence is the documented exception.
- [x] **Human gates stay human**: plan-approval is person-only, unreplaceable, and guards the phase exit.
- [x] **Agnostic**.

## Risks & Mitigations
| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| A lane reads hostile item or RFC text unsandboxed | steered within the allowed helpers | default mode: only hefesto's helpers run unprompted; none clears a block; the item and RFC stay delimited data; documented |
| A typed name is not authentication | a model types a name | the clear is a permission dialog every time (never allowlisted); refused in workers; recorded |
| The RFC changes after approval | build drifts from the approved design | the hash pin blocks the build until re-approval |
| `--stage all` holds the orchestrator ~40 min | gates wait | documented as a catch-up pass; the loops are the rhythm |

## Revision 3 (binding; re-review 2026-10-19)
1. **N1** No route back to the planner: a changed RFC is resolved by the person updating spec/plan/tasks
   in the item folder, re-pinning with `ledger.sh record <id> --rfc` (dialog; ask rule) and re-approving.
2. **N2** Lane allowlist = read-only/needed subcommands only: `status-board.sh --detailed|--check|--item |--item-rfc|--item-kind|--item-repo`,
   `ledger.sh board|list|next|show|metrics|register|block|publish|escalate`, `session-launch.sh`,
   `speckit-helper.sh`. No `pr-watch.sh`, no `status-board.sh --mark`.
3. **N3** The launcher also emits `permissions.ask` for `ledger.sh unblock|record|claim|advance|handoff`
   (both roots, single and doubled slash): ask beats any inherited allow. Case 12 asserts them.
4. **N4** The RFC is resolved from the board top (`HEFESTO_BOARD_TOP` / board ctx), `rfc_dir` validated
   with the same regex (relative, no `..`). The plan launch embeds the RFC text in the prompt as
   comment-stripped, nonce-delimited data (≤ 100 KB, else refused naming the size) and pins
   `.source.rfc = {path, sha256}` *at launch*. The approval refuses when the current hash differs from the
   pin; the implement launch refuses and blocks `human:plan-approval` when it differs.
5. **N5** `register`: stderr captured for the refusal message; temp file under `trap`; an existing entry
   is left untouched (exit 0, "already registered"), so it can never re-hash an edited item.
6. **N6** The gauge reads `<workspace.current_dir>/.claude/project-status.json` (no git call); missing or
   invalid → 40.
7. Extra cases: re-register of an edited item leaves `body_sha256`; RFC edited between plan run and
   approval → approval refused; `rfc_dir` `..`/absolute refused; `--print` has no pr-watch/`--mark`
   allow and has the ask rules.
